articles.detail: 5 cycles, all completed; 11/8/7/7/14 stories selected against targets of 11/12/13/15/15 and all 47 published (10 of them slugged 2026-10-09, so 38 count as today's); avg 8 per cycle by date; 0 quarantined

experiment: Skipped. No experiment is active, and the pause gate (`noNewExperimentsUntil` 2026-11-05) bars a new one; nothing was evaluated or changed.
weakestArea: Volume and category balance on a thin Saturday feed: the selector stopped at 8, 7 and 7 stories against targets of 12, 13 and 15 rather than pad, so economy fell to 7 (under its floor of 3 in three cycles, with no multi-source economy story in four of five feeds) and politics took 53% of output. Science is 3 against 5 a day (1, 0, 1, 0, 1 against a floor of 2), by design: the feed held journal manuscripts and boilerplate, not findings. US datelines at 26% and Latin America at 3% are each one story off target on a 38-article day, and the Latin America reading misses one of its two datelines.
watching: Iran: Hormuz oil exports plunged and the Guards claimed a mine hit a tanker, while Putin relayed Tehran's terms for ending the war to Trump.
Saudi Arabia: a missile hit Riyadh airport, a day after airlines halted flights there.
Red Sea: rival claims over Bab al-Mandab collided.
Ukraine: Trump said he wants a new Ukrainian leader, Miami talks excluded Russia, Seoul recalled its Kyiv ambassador and Moscow claimed a strike on a Kyiv data centre.
India: Delhi locked down a protest and police detained its founder and opposition leaders.
Pakistan: Rawalpindi banned gatherings and Balochistan reported 10 killed.
UAE: authorities detailed the radicalisation of the flydubai co-pilot.
Nigeria: gunfire hit an opposition rally in Enugu.
coverageGaps: Three cycles ran well short of target (8 of 12, 7 of 13, 7 of 15) because the feeds held 3 to 6 multi-source stories and mostly unusable niche items.
Economy was under its floor at 10:00 (2), 14:00 (1) and 18:00 (1); the multi-source economy floor was met in no cycle.

Science was under its floor in four of five cycles, and Nature, Quanta, New Scientist, STAT, SciDev.Net and Carbon Brief supplied nothing usable; the three science stories came from 404 Media, Ars Technica and The New York Times.
Tech was 0 of 3 at 14:00 and 1 of 3 at 18:00, with nothing from Ars Technica, The Register, The Decoder, 404 Media or Hacker News in the later feeds.

Latin America reads 3% in the metrics (one dateline counted), though the day's 38 carry two, Brasília and Ensenada, which would be 5%; the metric appears not to place Ensenada in Mexico. The selector also skipped the Antofagasta copper strike in Chile because Bloomberg fetches had been failing.

Four stories rest on state media alone, all on the Russia and Ukraine file: the Donetsk resettlement, Putin relaying Iran's terms, the Kyiv data-centre strike claim and the South Korean ambassador's departure.
Europe had 5 datelines against 11 yesterday, and Africa 4.
context: All five cycles completed, averaging 786s (selector 148s, writer 124s, editor 59s), with no repeat of Friday's weekly-usage-limit abort. The shortfalls are supply, not a fault: the selector declined to pad a weekend feed, and the 22:00 cycle recovered to 14 of 15. Top-source share fell from 26% to 11% (Al Jazeera and TASS, 4 articles each), so yesterday's breach did not persist; multi-source eased from 48% to 34%, still over target. The MercoPress addition to CURATED_SOURCES remains the first experiment to run once the gate lifts on 2026-11-05, after its Event Registry URI is verified.
